description: Hey guys, we're doing the Build a Junior Astronaut challenge. Feel free to join if you have experience with game development (we will likely be making the game in Java). Thanks!
summary: For our project, we developed a resource-management survival video game, and we pulled recorded and archived numbers from the provided APIs to enhance the realism of the game. It addressed the challenge by establishing a theoretical Martian outpost and breaking it down into different aspects, tasks, and resources for players to manage, such as food, power, radiation, and temperature. This is important because it teaches players about the importance of resource management, especially through the two features of energy and time. Each action players take to survive and prevent health from being lost in the game sacrifices both energy and time that could be reallocated elsewhere, and so they must choose which course of action provides the most benefit, mimicking real-life decisions that would be made by astronauts in similar situations.
details: Our project was developed almost entirely in Java, with minimal use of HTML to create a website to make it more accessible. The way our project works is by breaking down different tasks around a theoretical Martian outpost into a video game. Players are made to maintain their health by managing certain tasks around the outpost. The main factors are food, radiation, temperature, and power. Some systems require power, such as greenhouse lights or temperature control. Some tasks require the player to be outside of radiation protection, which will negatively impact their health. Energy production, radiation, and temperature can all be affected by sources such as seasons or solar events, which players will also have to account for, often by sacrificing some systems or spending time carrying out a task. The game has impact and benefits the intended younger audience by allowing them to experience a scenario in which every choice has a risk and a benefit, putting them in a situation similar to what real astronauts would face in these types of scenario. It teaches them to analyze what their choices are, what they stand to gain and lose, and which choice to make given the situation. Some factors we considered while developing the project were realism and simplicity. We used the public APIs provided by the challenge to research past conditions on Mars to help model a realistic environment, pulling both average numbers on climate and radiation data to model typical conditions, while also pulling data from solar events such as solar storms, to model conditions during these events, to add variation and difficulty to the game. We also understood the target audience, and tailored our game design to be simple, both in terms of game mechanics and UI design.
